# Get your Workbench Bots

The starter team has four focused roles. Each recipient adds their own copies in their own Grok Bot account. No project files, account sessions, conversation history or credentials from the publisher are included.

## Add the templates

Open a starter below, inspect its description, then choose **Add to Grok Bot** if you agree to the provider's third-party Bot terms. Repeat only for the roles you want. The [template catalog](../bots/templates.json) also records these links and their profile hashes.

| Bot | Best first assignment |
| --- | --- |
| **[Add Research](https://x.ai/bot/6SgIaeo7NYBGrKGPRoTwE)** | Check supplied public sources and return cited facts and uncertainty. |
| **[Add Systems](https://x.ai/bot/kcMHwterc33F-1FjGGnP3)** | Map dependencies, assumptions, failure cases and useful verification. |
| **[Add Design](https://x.ai/bot/wbLs8l_Xpej3rH9ewWycd)** | Improve clarity and usability without claiming unperformed testing. |
| **[Add Critic](https://x.ai/bot/WccXiAjk8dxdQvLtPqpAA)** | Challenge unsupported claims and identify missing evidence. |

These templates contain neutral descriptions and instructions. They have no bundled skills, routines, plugins, private memories or scheduled tasks. The public catalog records the description hash and the date the landing page was checked. Provider availability and terms can change.

If a link is unavailable, an administrator disables template sharing, or you prefer to inspect all text first, use the copyable setup below. A working Grok Bot account is required in either case; no subscription or credits are included.

## Copyable setup

Open [setup-team.txt](../prompts/setup-team.txt), copy the full text and paste it into an existing Bot in your own account. It asks the Bot to create or reuse the four exact names, apply their supplied descriptions, create an **Agent Workbench** group and report the result. It asks for no account, billing or permission changes.

The JSON in `bots/catalog.json` is our readable catalog format. It is **not** an undocumented native import file. If your app cannot create Bots from the setup request, create each Bot manually and paste the description from `bots/*.md`.

After adding individual template copies, either create the group manually with the four Bots or ask an existing Bot: “Create a group named Agent Workbench using the existing Workbench Research, Workbench Systems, Workbench Design and Workbench Critic Bots. Reuse exact matches; do not create duplicates or start work.”

## Check the setup

1. Confirm each name and full description matches [the role catalog](../bots/catalog.json).
2. Confirm no unexpected skills, routines, attachments or plugins were added. Do not grant extra permissions to make this starter task work.
3. Confirm the group contains the intended roles. Keep the coordinator and final reviewer as separate responsibilities in your workflow.
4. Start with public information. Bots within your own account may share that account's cloud computer and sessions; they are not separate security sandboxes.

## Run the first task

Copy [first-task.txt](../prompts/first-task.txt), replace its two public source URL placeholders and set the requested task details. Send it to **Workbench Research**. The intended sequence is Research → Systems → Design → Critic, with a group delta before each explicit handoff and no acknowledgment loop.

Read the actual group transcript. Check that the task ID, named sources, acceptance criteria and deadline survive each handoff. Stop the task if a Bot exceeds its scope, starts a loop or reaches the budget. Prompts specify the limits; they do not enforce remote concurrency or turn counts.

The final output is a candidate. Have your independent lead reviewer verify citations and claims against the original criteria. Run code or interface checks in your own project when relevant. The local `npm run demo` is an offline state-machine example, not a test of your new Grok Bot copies.

## Change or remove a role

Edit your own copies and keep your catalog and prompts consistent. Shared template updates do not establish that your existing copy changed; inspect it. You can remove unused Bots or the group through the app's normal controls. No recurring task needs to be stopped for this starter kit because none is created.

Official references: [Grok Bot overview](https://cursor.com/docs/grok-bot) and [working with Bots and sharing templates](https://cursor.com/docs/grok-bot/work).

# API and CLI

Requires Node.js 22 or newer. The module uses only Node built-ins. It stores JSON locally and makes no network or model calls.

## Start a store

```js
const { createStore, hash, POLICY, POLICY_HASH } = require('./lib/index.cjs');
const store = createStore({ stateFile: '.agent-evolution/state.json' });
store.init();
const state = store.readState();
```

To begin with an existing configuration, initialize a new store with `store.init({ artifacts: yourCurrentArtifacts })`. This seeds the trusted initial baseline once; it does not replace an already initialized store. The initial baseline is a valid rollback target, including after the first promotion.

The fixed policy requires at least three distinct training cases, at least one held-out case, a higher-is-better score, and at least **0.01 score units of improvement in every case**. A registration may set a stricter threshold. This is an absolute score difference, not a one-percent improvement or a token-savings claim.

The policy is protected through the supported API. An operator who can replace the package or edit its files remains outside that boundary. See [Security](../SECURITY.md).

## 1. Propose an editable configuration

```js
const proposed = store.propose({
  proposer: 'research-proposer',
  baseVersion: state.activeVersion,
  baseRevision: state.revision,
  artifacts: {
    instructions: { research: 'Separate sourced facts from inferences.' },
    prompts: { research: 'Include counterevidence and unresolved gaps.' },
    skills: { evidenceReview: { output: ['finding', 'source', 'limitation'] } },
    routing: { publicResearch: ['research-worker', 'reviewer'] }
  }
});
```

`artifacts` is a complete candidate snapshot. Preserve the active values you want to retain; do not assume omitted fields are merged. Only `instructions`, `prompts`, `skills`, and `routing` are editable top-level kinds. These are data, not executable skill installers or provider registrations. Control fields and oversized or unsupported data are rejected.

The result supplies `candidateId`, `candidateHash`, `baseVersion`, `baselineHash`, and `policyHash`. Keep these values; do not derive trusted bindings from a worker's returned claims.

## 2. Register evaluation before collecting results

```js
const cases = [
  { id: 'research-a', split: 'train', datasetHash: hash('synthetic case A') },
  { id: 'research-b', split: 'train', datasetHash: hash('synthetic case B') },
  { id: 'research-c', split: 'train', datasetHash: hash('synthetic case C') },
  { id: 'research-held-out', split: 'holdout', datasetHash: hash('synthetic held-out case') }
];
const evaluation = store.registerEvaluation({
  candidateId: proposed.candidateId,
  candidateHash: proposed.candidateHash,
  baselineHash: proposed.baselineHash,
  policyHash: proposed.policyHash,
  metric: { name: 'quality', direction: 'higher-is-better', minimumImprovement: 0.01 },
  cases
});
```

These strings are illustrative fixtures. In a real evaluation, hash the exact selected dataset representation and keep held-out material outside the proposer's access. IDs and dataset hashes must be distinct. Registration cannot prove dataset quality, independence, or secrecy.

## 3. Submit complete paired evidence

The trusted evaluator now runs the baseline and candidate on each registered case using the same rubric. Record the resulting values:

```js
const evidence = store.recordEvidence({
  candidateId: proposed.candidateId,
  evaluationId: evaluation.evaluationId,
  candidateHash: proposed.candidateHash,
  baselineHash: proposed.baselineHash,
  policyHash: proposed.policyHash,
  cases: cases.map(item => ({
    ...item,
    baselineScore: 0.80,
    candidateScore: 0.83,
    declaredImprovement: 0.03
  }))
});
```

The values above are **synthetic**, not model measurements. Every registered ID, split and dataset hash must match, with no duplicate or missing result. Scores and improvements must be finite and consistent. A passing aggregate cannot hide a failed individual case.

The engine validates submitted data; the trusted evaluator must establish its truth. Store detailed outputs and reproducible evaluation commands in your own evidence system.

## 4. Review, then promote

After inspecting the real outputs, an independently authorized reviewer supplies the exact candidate, evidence and policy bindings:

```js
const reviewed = store.review({
  candidateId: proposed.candidateId,
  evidenceId: evidence.evidenceId,
  candidateHash: proposed.candidateHash,
  evidenceHash: evidence.evidenceHash,
  policyHash: proposed.policyHash,
  reviewer: 'independent-reviewer',
  approved: true
});
const promoted = store.promote({
  candidateId: proposed.candidateId,
  evidenceId: evidence.evidenceId,
  reviewId: reviewed.reviewId
});
```

The reviewer name must differ from the proposer. That string comparison is not authentication. Your host verifies identity and authorization. `approved: false` rejects the candidate; it is not a retry switch to overwrite until the record says yes.

Promotion makes the candidate the store's active local configuration. A stale base or mismatched approval is rejected. Use the separate staged methods when connecting an evaluator or remote reviewer, so each returned record is checked against the original trusted bindings.

## 5. Export and roll back

```js
store.exportActive({
  destination: '.agent-evolution/export/active.json',
  exportRoot: '.agent-evolution/export'
});
// Restore a known prior version after an observed regression:
store.rollback({ version: previousVersion });
```

Create the export directory first. The destination must be contained within `exportRoot` and meet the filesystem guards. Export writes configuration data; it does not update a remote bot. Re-export after rollback and verify the host that consumes it.

`previousVersion` must come from trusted store history. The [complete demo](../examples/demo.cjs) shows promotion, export, and rollback with concrete values and synthetic scores.

## CLI commands

Every command requires an explicit state path. The published command is `agent-evolution`; from a source checkout use `node bin/agent-evolution.cjs`.

| Command | Additional arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | None |
| `show` | None |
| `propose` | `--input proposal.json` |
| `register-evaluation` | `--input evaluation.json` |
| `evidence` | `--input evidence.json` |
| `review` | `--input review.json` |
| `promote` | `--input promotion.json` |
| `rollback` | `--version VERSION` |
| `export` | `--destination FILE --root DIRECTORY` |

For example:

```bash
node bin/agent-evolution.cjs show --state .agent-evolution/state.json
node bin/agent-evolution.cjs propose --state .agent-evolution/state.json --input proposal.json
```

Input JSON uses the corresponding method's fields shown above. Successful commands print JSON; rejected operations print an error and exit nonzero. Do not retry a rejected promotion by altering its evidence or claimed identity.

## Operational bounds

This is a bounded local store, not a distributed database or a security sandbox. Concurrent writes use a local lock, while version bindings prevent stale candidates from becoming active. Keep the state directory under trusted control. Back up the state and exported versions; inspect an abandoned lock and its process before taking any recovery action.

The engine limits artifact size, nesting, evaluation cases, candidate count and history growth. Hitting a limit stops the operation. It does not silently discard history or run a cleanup daemon.

# Agent Pipeline **A local coordination kit for taking AI work from a clear task to a checked, deliverable result.** For developers and teams using several AI tools who need accountable handoffs, recoverable changes, and a finish line. **[Run the local demo](#try-it-in-five-commands)** · [Download v1.0.0](https://github.com/Wassimyounes01/agent-pipeline/releases/download/v1.0.0/agent-pipeline-v1.0.0.zip) · [Read the whole pipeline](docs/pipeline.md) ## Why use it? Your coding assistant produces a patch. A research bot spots a missing requirement. Another agent changes a shared assumption. Which result is still valid—and what proves the final output works? Agent Pipeline connects a task contract, bounded worker selection, dependency-aware coordination, review evidence, and controlled configuration improvement. It includes runnable local mechanisms and original prompts you can adapt to your own tools. | Problem | Mechanism included | Practical benefit | | --- | --- | --- | | Handoffs lose the original goal | Source and acceptance bindings | A result stays attached to the task it addresses | | Workers repeat an uncertain attempt | Conservative routing and reconciliation | The router tells the coordinator to wait instead of dispatching a duplicate | | An upstream correction leaves stale approvals | Workbench dependency invalidation | Recheck the affected work while preserving independent branches | | Prompt changes accumulate without evidence | Evolution registration, paired scores, review and rollback | Adopt a version through a repeatable process | | A polished README hides a broken download | Publishing skill and consumer checks | Verify what the next user actually receives | These controls validate supplied data and local state. Your host still supplies authentic reviews, real evaluations, provider access, secure storage, and permission to act. ## Try it in five commands Requires **Node.js 22+** and Git. No package install, API key, or account is needed for the local examples. ```sh git clone https://github.com/Wassimyounes01/agent-pipeline.git cd agent-pipeline npm test npm run demo npm run lab ``` Alternatively, download the ZIP above, extract it, and run the final three commands in its root folder. The demo uses **synthetic inputs and review attestations** to exercise the combined lifecycle. The lab exercises correction and recovery. Neither runs a live model or measures AI quality or token savings. See [verification](docs/verification.md) for checks and trust limits. ## One task, connected stages ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Define task and acceptance] --> B[Retrieve relevant context] B --> C[Choose bounded worker] C --> D[Receive candidate and evidence] D --> E[Verify and independently review] E --> F{Accepted?} F -->|No| G[Record failure and revise affected work] G --> C F -->|Yes| H[Deliver through authorized host] H --> I[Check the delivered result] I --> J[Record a candidate lesson] J --> K[Evaluate configuration change] K --> L[Promote or retain current version] ``` The local runtime handles parts of this flow; the coordinator carries out the rest. [See exactly what is automated](docs/pipeline.md#execution-boundary). ## Real-life scenarios — illustrative **A public API migration.** A research specialist checks the public migration guide. A coding worker drafts the change. An independent reviewer checks behavior and compatibility. If a source assumption changes, dependent work is reopened before delivery. Use this when the handoffs and dependencies warrant more than one worker. **A repository launch.** A coding worker makes the package runnable; the Design and Critic roles examine its explanation and claims. The publishing skill guides examples, before/after material, accessible diagrams, sanitization and a fresh download check. Use this when other people need to install the output without your local setup. **Improving a research agent.** A worker proposes clearer evidence instructions. A trusted evaluator compares the baseline and candidate on preregistered cases, including a held-out case. A separate reviewer approves eligible evidence before promotion. Roll back if later consumer checks expose a regression. Use this for controlled configuration changes, not model training. ## Before and after — illustrative | Before: disconnected chats and manual prompt edits | After: this kit in a configured host | | --- | --- | | Paste the full history into every tool | Send a bounded task and relevant source bindings | | Retry because a worker has not returned | Reconcile the recorded attempt before another dispatch | | Treat a confident answer as completed work | Keep candidate, review and acceptance distinct | | Reopen every task after one correction | Invalidate affected dependencies and retain independent work | | Keep an appealing new prompt after one example | Register evaluation cases, review paired evidence, then promote | | Publish whatever works in the source tree | Test the same artifact a new consumer downloads | This is a workflow comparison, not a measured claim of faster work or lower cost. ## Choose the right worker | Capability | Typical assignment | | --- | --- | | Lead planner / reviewer | Acceptance contract, difficult decisions, independent final review | | External coding worker, such as Cursor | Bounded code drafts and focused repairs | | Native coder | Private code or unavailable external-worker fallback | | Native analyst | Tool-dependent synthesis, audits, public-research fallback | | Native small worker | Small structured transformations | | Grok Bot Research / Systems / Design / Critic | Eligible public-source research and additional perspectives | | Local tools | Searches, checks, hashes, packaging | Model names are configurable examples. No subscription, remote bot, or premium model is included. Read [routing and Grok fallback](docs/providers.md). ## Included, not just linked | Directory | What you receive | | --- | --- | | [components/workbench](components/workbench/README.md) | Team state, dependencies, bounded briefs, recovery lab, four Bot profiles | | [components/evolution](components/evolution/README.md) | Local configuration proposals, evidence gates, promotion, export and rollback | | [lib](lib/) · [examples](examples/) | Routing composition and executable combined example | | [prompts](prompts/genesis.md) | Original Genesis execution prompt and task contract | | [skills/github-repo-publishing](skills/github-repo-publishing/SKILL.md) | Portable repo design and verified publishing skill | | [docs](docs/pipeline.md) | End-to-end workflow, provider boundaries, white-label setup and verification | ## Where it fits—and where it does not Use this kit when explicit coordination and evidence are worth the overhead. A single small edit may be better handled by one assistant and a focused check. An existing production agent framework may already provide durable execution, authentication and integrations this kit deliberately leaves to the host. **This release does not launch Cursor or Grok, create accounts, send email, deploy applications, run schedules, authenticate reviewers, train model weights, or guarantee savings.** The adapters and operating instructions in a private installation are not exported credentials or portable integrations. [Integration guide](docs/providers.md) · [Make it yours](docs/white-label.md) · [Security](SECURITY.md) · [License](LICENSE)

# Agent Evolution **A controlled self-modification layer for agent instructions, skills, and routing.** For teams that already use agents and want a repeatable way to evaluate, adopt, and undo configuration changes. Let an agent suggest a better configuration. Test it against the current version, review the evidence, and make the change active only when it passes. Keep the previous version available for rollback. [Download the complete pipeline](https://github.com/Wassimyounes01/agent-pipeline/releases/latest) · [Try the demo](#try-it-locally) · [Integration guide](docs/integration.md) · [Trust boundaries](SECURITY.md) ## Why use it? An agent notices that its research summaries often omit counterevidence. Updating its prompt is easy. Knowing whether the update helped, whether it hurt another task, and how to undo it takes more work. Agent Evolution supplies that missing change process: a candidate tied to its starting version, preregistered test cases, paired evidence, independent review, a recorded promotion, and rollback. Your host supplies the agents and real evaluations; this package manages the configuration lifecycle. | You need… | What this adds | | --- | --- | | Changes you can explain | A proposal tied to the version it replaces | | Evidence before adoption | Separate evaluation registration before results are recorded | | A fixed evaluation set | At least three distinct training cases and one held-out case, with complete paired results | | A review step the proposer cannot simply skip | A named reviewer, separate from the proposer, bound to the candidate and evidence | | Recoverable configuration updates | Versioned promotion and rollback to a known prior version | | Freedom to choose your agent stack | A local CommonJS API, JSON CLI, and editable neutral role templates | The engine checks the consistency and completeness of submitted evidence. It does **not** independently authenticate a reviewer or prove that a score was measured. Keep those responsibilities in a trusted host. ## Before and after These are **illustrative workflows**, not measured customer results. | Situation | Ad hoc prompt editing | With Agent Evolution | | --- | --- | --- | | A research agent misses opposing evidence | Append another instruction and hope | Propose the change, compare registered cases, then review before activation | | A new writing skill improves one example but hurts another | Keep the appealing example | Reject the candidate when any required case fails the improvement gate | | A routing change performs poorly after rollout | Reconstruct yesterday's configuration | Restore a recorded prior version and export that configuration | | Two workers propose changes from the same starting point | Apply both and risk overwriting work | Check the candidate's base version and revision before promotion | ## Real-life scenarios (illustrative) **Research teams.** A research bot proposes a requirement to separate sourced facts, inferences, and counterevidence. The evaluator compares the current and proposed instructions on distinct research tasks, including a held-out case. A reviewer examines the actual findings before a configuration is promoted. Better formatting alone is not proof of better research. **Support knowledge assistants.** A team refines a skill for retrieving the right troubleshooting article. Evaluation uses synthetic or appropriately protected customer scenarios. The trusted support application continues to own authentication, personal data access, escalation rules, and permission to send replies. **Coding teams.** A worker proposes clearer test-writing instructions or a different routing configuration. The host evaluates real acceptance criteria and includes failed attempts in any efficiency measurement. Promotion changes local configuration; installing it into a production coding harness is a separate integration step. See [the integration guide](docs/integration.md) for where these responsibilities live. ## The controlled loop ```mermaid flowchart TD P[Propose a change] --> E[Register evaluation] E --> T[Record paired results] T --> R{Evidence and review pass?} R -->|Yes| A[Promote local config] R -->|No| K[Keep active version] A --> X[Export to your host] X --> M[Observe real tasks] M -->|Regression| B[Roll back] B --> X classDef candidate fill:#e8f4ff,stroke:#397db0,color:#15314b classDef active fill:#e7f5eb,stroke:#43815c,color:#193e29 classDef hold fill:#fff2dc,stroke:#ae7c34,color:#573c18 class P,E,T candidate class A,X active class K,B hold ``` The engine modifies data through its API. Candidate artifacts cannot edit the promotion policy or evaluator through those operations. Your filesystem and runtime must enforce the corresponding access boundary. ## Try it locally Requires **Node.js 22 or newer**. No runtime dependencies, account, API key, GPU, or background service is needed for the included demo. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Wassimyounes01/agent-pipeline.git cd agent-pipeline/components/evolution npm test npm run demo ``` The demo exercises proposal, evaluation registration, paired results, review, promotion, export, and rollback with **synthetic evidence**. It demonstrates lifecycle behavior; it does not measure the quality or token cost of a real model. For your own state file: ```bash node bin/agent-evolution.cjs init --state .agent-evolution/state.json ``` Use the [API and CLI guide](docs/api.md) for the exact input shapes. The release ZIP contains the same source, tests, examples, and templates. ## What changes—and what stays with your host | Editable data | Outside the modification loop | | --- | --- | | Instructions and prompt text | Tool permissions and external action authorization | | Skill definitions | Credentials, privacy controls and customer data access | | Routing configuration | Spending limits and account eligibility | | Active configuration version | Evaluators, reviewer identity and promotion policy | Prompt text is not a security boundary. A malicious proposal can contain dangerous instructions even if it is structurally valid. Review content and enforce permissions outside the candidate's control. ## Grok Bot, Cursor, and your existing team Use the [four neutral role templates](bots) to divide proposal, evaluation, critique, and integration work. They are editable prompts, not pre-created remote accounts or authenticated reviewers. Grok Bot can contribute a candidate through its supported app workflow. Cursor or another coding agent can help implement and test a host adapter. This package runs the local lifecycle and exports configuration; it does **not** silently update a live Grok Bot or assume a headless Grok API. The [integration guide](docs/integration.md) includes the application boundary. ## A reusable publishing skill The release also includes [GitHub Repo Publishing](../../skills/github-repo-publishing/SKILL.md): a portable skill and Genesis prompt for designing a repository page around real use cases, before-and-after explanations, readable visuals, and verified quickstarts. Keep the skill folder together when installing it in your agent's skill directory. ## When to choose something simpler A single prompt edited occasionally may need only Git and a few tests. A full hosted experiment platform may be a better fit when you need authenticated multi-user approval, distributed execution, dashboards, or managed telemetry. Agent Evolution fits a local or host-controlled workflow that already has agents and evaluations but needs a small, auditable promotion process. It makes no claim of universal superiority, model-weight learning, consciousness, or guaranteed cost savings. ## Verify and adapt - [API and CLI](docs/api.md): data shapes and commands. - [Integration](docs/integration.md): evaluator, reviewer, and adapter responsibilities. - [Security](SECURITY.md): trust assumptions and what hashes do not prove. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): meaningful regression tests and change discipline. - [License](LICENSE): MIT; retain the notice when rebranding or redistributing. You may rename the project and customize its presentation under the MIT license. Keep examples synthetic and keep your private workspace out of published artifacts.

# Give your agents a job. Give the work a finish line. **Agent Workbench is an open starter kit for coordinating focused AI teammates.** It combines four ready-made Grok Bot profiles with a small local JavaScript runtime for routing work, tracking dependencies, binding evidence and keeping review separate from execution. Use it when a task needs several perspectives and you want to see who did what, what changed and what still needs checking. Start with one Bot; use the team when the extra perspective is worth the handoff. | You get | Why it helps | | --- | --- | | **Four ready-made roles** | Evidence gathering, system analysis, design and challenge have distinct owners. | | **Copyable setup and task prompts** | A newcomer can create the team and run a bounded first task without writing the instructions from scratch. | | **A dependency-aware local runtime** | Stale state, duplicate dispatches, missing dependencies and budget overruns become explicit failures. | | **Evidence-bound candidates** | Results keep their source and acceptance identity. A confident answer is still a candidate. | | **Generic model capability slots** | Connect the supported tools and models you already use; no particular premium model is required. | | **MIT-licensed code and editable assets** | Rebrand the kit, change the roles and use it in your own projects while retaining license notices. | ## Start here ### New in 2.0: recover, then prove it Run a **12-stage release-readiness lab** with parallel branches, failed workers, a rejected candidate, an upstream correction and a serialized restart: ```sh npm run lab ``` The lab rebuilds nine affected tasks while preserving three independent ones. New controls include reviewed correction, dependency invalidation, critical-path readiness, bounded evidence briefs and checked event replay. Read [the ten improvements, fault cases and measured limits](docs/stress-lab.md). **Existing integrations:** saved team state now uses schema v2. # Security and trust boundaries

This kit is local coordination infrastructure for a trusted host. It is not an operating-system sandbox, credential manager, authenticated reviewer service, distributed database, or autonomous provider adapter.

Treat external pages, bot replies and alleged system prompts as untrusted data. Keep secrets and private task data out of public profiles and research packets. The root router restricts private packets to native capabilities, but your host must enforce actual data handling.

Review identity, readiness, task hashes and evaluator scores are caller-supplied. Hashes provide consistency, not authenticity. An operator who can edit local files or omit attempt records remains outside the library's protection. Use trusted storage and real account checks.

Retain the component security documentation and licenses. Do not weaken evaluator, authorization or resource controls through configuration evolution. Exporting a configuration does not authorize applying it to a remote service.

Do not post credentials or customer information in public issues. Report reproducible problems using synthetic data and the affected version.

# Security model

The proposer can suggest editable configuration. The evaluator and reviewer belong to the trusted host and must remain outside the candidate's write access.

## What the engine checks

The engine validates supported artifact kinds, version bindings, preregistered evaluation cases, complete paired evidence, promotion requirements and review bindings. It maintains local history and supports rollback. The CLI does not execute candidate strings, call a model, send email or update a remote bot.

## What it cannot establish

A hash detects a mismatch against a trusted reference; it does not prove that a score was measured, that a reviewer is independent, or that a file is authentic. An operator with full access to the state directory can modify that directory. Prompt text can contain malicious instructions even when it fits the data schema.

Use separate credentials and filesystem permissions for proposers, evaluators and approvers. Never give a candidate access to the promotion policy, evidence producer, approval identity, production credentials, or the external runtime's permission controls. Enforce email authorization, privacy, budget and tool restrictions in the host runtime. Do not rely on a prompt to enforce them.

Do not feed public examples with private correspondence, tokens or customer records. Use synthetic fixtures for development. Validate the destination and content before applying an exported configuration to a live service. Start with a canary task and restore the previous version if it regresses.

## Reporting

For a security concern, use the repository's private vulnerability reporting feature if it is enabled. Otherwise contact the repository maintainer through an available private channel. Never post credentials or private customer data in a public issue.

# Security and data boundaries

Use synthetic or explicitly public input for the starter Bots. The router relies on the caller's public/private classification. URL validation rejects several non-public host forms, but it does not resolve DNS, inspect redirects or scan free text for secrets. Inspect the complete outgoing packet yourself; a syntactically valid public URL or a public input label is not proof that the content is safe to share.

The runtime does not execute provider calls, authenticate reviewers, inspect evidence files or sandbox an agent. Bot profiles do not override the provider's permissions. Bots within one Grok Bot account can share that account's cloud computer and sessions; a separate recipient's template copy runs in that recipient's account. See the [official sharing documentation](https://cursor.com/docs/grok-bot/work).

Do not post credentials, customer data, exploit payloads containing private data, or conversation transcripts in public issues. Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting option if it is enabled. Otherwise, open a minimal issue requesting a private contact channel, without the sensitive details.

For a suspected defect, include the version, expected boundary, a synthetic reproducer and the observed result. Treat generated findings as hypotheses until reproduced. No paid bug bounty or response-time guarantee is offered.

# From task to verified output

## 1. Form a task contract

State the requested outcome, relevant source, acceptance criteria, affected consumers, ownership, dependencies, budget, and stopping point. Resolve the owning files through your own project index. The kit does not include the author's private workspace index.

Use [the task template](../prompts/task-contract.md). Small tasks should use proportional checks and may need no delegation.

## 2. Retrieve and reuse narrowly

Retrieve a few relevant prior attributes or components, not entire transcripts. Preserve provenance and distinguish an approved design from an untested idea. A file index is not proof that its contents have been audited.

## 3. Route a bounded packet

Use task kind, data classification, fresh readiness and prior-attempt state to select a capability. Code can use an eligible external coding worker or a native coder. Public research can use an eligible Grok Bot, then a native analyst, then the lead. Private inputs stay native in this routing layer.

A routing decision is a proposal to the coordinator. [Provider integration](providers.md) describes dispatch, identity binding and reconciliation.

## 4. Coordinate dependencies

The Workbench core represents task owners, dependencies, candidates, review attestations and bounded transitions. Its brief builder can supply a compact task-specific projection. One integrator owns shared interfaces.

Keep actual evidence outside conversational confidence. The host verifies that claimed source and evidence hashes identify the files it inspected.

## 5. Adjust on evidence

A failed test, correction or changed assumption can invalidate downstream work. Preserve the original failure and name a reproducer. Review a correction, reopen affected tasks, repair the cause and rerun affected checks.

The bundled Workbench lab demonstrates recovery and preservation of independent branches. It is a local fixture, not a live multi-model benchmark.

## 6. Verify and review

Check the behavior that matters to the consumer. Frontend work may require rendering, interactions, responsiveness and accessibility; backend work may require contracts, state integrity, security and error paths. A release needs an actual consumer download test.

Use a reviewer independent of the implementation when the contract calls for it. The kit checks caller-supplied review bindings; it does not authenticate the person or model behind a reviewer label.

## 7. Deliver and verify delivery

Use the host's authorized publishing, deployment or messaging path. Preserve existing authorization; do not infer new authority from a prompt file. Then inspect the actual delivered artifact or affected consumer.

The [publishing skill](../skills/github-repo-publishing/SKILL.md) applies to repository pages and releases. It does not deploy your application.

## 8. Record a candidate lesson

Record trigger, observed gap, proposed invariant, counterexample, test, evidence and rollback condition. Successful completion can justify a candidate lesson, not immediate global adoption.

The Evolution core accepts editable configuration snapshots. Promotion requires preregistered distinct cases, paired improvement evidence and a separate reviewer attestation. It stores and exports local configuration. Your trusted host applies it to a real agent and verifies the resulting behavior.

## Execution boundary

| Layer | Runs locally in the kit | Supplied by your host |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routing | Input validation and capability decision | Live readiness observations, actual dispatch, account eligibility |
| Coordination | Task-state transitions, dependency checks, evidence bindings | Real workers, secure durable storage, authentic evidence |
| Verification | Runnable regression suites and synthetic examples | Task-specific evaluation and independent reviewer execution |
| Evolution | Registration, evidence consistency, promotion and rollback | Real scores, protected evaluator, applying exported configuration |
| Delivery | Prompts and publishing instructions | GitHub credentials, deployment transport, explicit action authority |
| Learning | Versioned configuration lifecycle | Repeated real-task evidence and controlled integration |

No continuous service is installed. The libraries are not an OS sandbox or a distributed executor. Read [Security](../SECURITY.md).

## Reproduce a consumer check

## What this proves

Passing checks support the exercised local behavior on the recorded runtime. They do not prove live Grok/Cursor dispatch, reviewer identity, truthful evaluator scores, production deployment, savings, or general AI quality.

The workbench records coordinator-attested review evidence; Evolution validates supplied paired scores and bindings. A trusted host must actually perform and protect the corresponding operations.

# Connect your own tools

The release is **transport-neutral**. It makes local routing decisions and exposes component APIs; it does not launch remote models. A host can be a human-operated workflow or an application with verified, authorized adapters.

## Recommended capability placement

Use your strongest suitable capability for planning and required review. Use a bounded external coding worker for suitable code; keep a native coding fallback. An analyst handles synthesis and tool-dependent investigation; a small worker handles narrow structured work.

A host may map these roles to Astra, Cursor Auto, Terra, Sol and Luna where available. These examples are not required products or promises of account availability. Use the same acceptance standard across worker choices.

## When to use Grok Bot

Use Research for public evidence, Systems for interfaces and failure cases, Design for a public page or explanation, and Critic for challenging a candidate. Start with the one role that addresses the gap.

The [four editable profiles and setup guide](../components/workbench/docs/grok-bot-setup.md) are included. Create or configure Bots in your own account through supported provider features. Shared public templates are optional. The source profiles work as copyable instructions even if a shared link becomes unavailable.

Do not put credentials, private customer information or unpublished local source into public-source Bot packets.

## Fallback and reconciliation

For eligible public research, the intended order is Grok Bot, native analyst, then lead. Code uses a coding route rather than a research Bot. A global pause stops routing.

Bind an attempt to its task, source and acceptance criteria. A confirmed failed or cancelled attempt permits fallback. Running, uncertain and completed attempts require reconciliation before further routing. Do not remove an old attempt record to make the task look new.

The router cannot discover whether you hid an attempt. Keep the attempt ledger in trusted host storage, reconcile provider state, and enforce actual slot reservation atomically before dispatch. A route recommendation does not reserve a remote worker.

## Host integration checklist

1. Generate fresh readiness from the real account and tool state; do not hardcode “ready.”
2. Build a bounded packet with complete relevant inputs and stable source/criteria bindings.
3. Run the local route decision.
4. Atomically record and reserve the authorized attempt in trusted storage.
5. Dispatch the complete returned `packet` through a supported provider interface. Its `taskContract` contains the exact task sources and criteria. Do not dispatch only a nested Workbench handoff or generic role template; that loses the task-specific contract.
6. Record actual success, failure, cancellation or uncertainty.
7. Inspect the returned candidate, execute acceptance checks and obtain required review.
8. Release capacity and deliver only through the authorized host.

See the runnable examples and exported API in [the package entry](../lib/index.cjs). Provider adapters are intentionally not included.

## Cost and quality measurement

Measure all native planner, worker, reviewer, retry and repair usage when optimizing native consumption. Track external subscriptions and spending separately. A smaller prompt is not automatically a measured membership saving.

Compare equivalent tasks with a preregistered quality rubric and held-out cases. Treat missing usage as unknown. This kit contains no current price catalog and claims no universal percentage improvement.

# Put the team to work

Start with public, non-sensitive material and one concrete deliverable. The examples below require your own source URLs; placeholders are not evidence.

## Turn a confusing product explanation into a quickstart

**Useful when:** the facts exist, but readers still do not understand the product or what to do first.

Give Research two public documentation pages. Ask for three cited facts and one caveat. Systems names the prerequisites and failure paths. Design writes a four-step quickstart. Critic challenges the strongest unsupported statement and returns a corrected candidate.

**Acceptance:** every product claim links to a supplied source; the steps have an explicit starting point and finish line; no pricing or performance claim is invented; the maintainer verifies the commands before publication.

**Example return:** “The draft called the group an isolation boundary. The documentation supports shared context, not isolation between these Bots. Replace that sentence and keep private sources outside this public task.”

This illustrates a correction, not a precomputed review of your product.

## Review a public API migration

**Useful when:** version changes can break more than the file being edited.

Use Research and Systems first. Supply the old and new public docs plus a sanitized interface description. Ask for a dependency map, changed contracts and concrete failure examples. Use Critic if a risky assumption remains; a Design stage is optional.

**Acceptance:** separate documented changes from hypotheses; identify affected consumers; propose executable checks; the code owner runs the actual migration tests. Use a suitable code worker for implementation outside the public Bot packet.

## Improve repository onboarding

**Useful when:** people can download the code but cannot run it reliably.

Systems traces the documented install/run path. Design rewrites it around the first successful result. Critic checks whether platform requirements, credentials and unsupported claims are clear.

**Acceptance:** a fresh checkout can run the exact documented commands; required access and costs are stated; links resolve; screenshots or test logs show what was actually checked.

## When one worker is enough

A typo, a short structured extraction or a known one-file fix rarely needs four Bots. Use the local tool or one eligible specialist, then do the relevant check. Handoff overhead is part of the task cost.

## A useful packet

```text
Task: public-onboarding-001
Outcome: a four-step quickstart, at most 150 words
Sources: [two exact public URLs]
Acceptance: source every factual product claim; expose prerequisites;
            separate observations from suggestions; return a candidate
Current owner: Workbench Research
Allowed chain: Research -> Systems -> Design -> Critic
Budget: four stages, three peer handoffs, ten minutes
Handoff: publish the group delta first; invoke only the next owner;
         send no further messages after invoking that owner
Stop: Critic returns final candidate; coordinator reviews; no publication
```

Define what the word “turn” means in your own integration. This kit's local state transitions, role stages and provider-internal inference turns are different counts.

# Connect the loop to an agent team

Agent Evolution manages local configuration versions. Your host supplies task execution, scoring, reviewer authorization, credentials and remote deployment.

## Responsibilities

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Proposer | Identify a specific failure and submit a bounded candidate based on the active version |
| Evaluator | Register the cases before collecting results; run the baseline and candidate against the same inputs and rubric |
| Reviewer | Inspect the actual artifacts and evidence, then approve or reject using a separate authorized identity |
| Integrator | Promote through the engine, export the active configuration, apply it through an authorized adapter, and observe a canary task |

The proposer must not control the evaluator, hidden test inputs, score records, review authority or the state directory's unrestricted write access. Separate operating-system identities or a trusted host service are needed when contributors are untrusted.

## A real evaluation

1. Define what the task must preserve before proposing a change.
2. Register distinct training cases and a held-out case with stable dataset hashes. Keep held-out material outside the proposer's access.
3. Run the current and proposed configurations against those cases using the same evaluation method.
4. Inspect generated artifacts as well as scores. Record failures, retries, missing telemetry and conditions that affected the comparison.
5. Submit the complete paired evidence. An independently authorized reviewer checks whether the evidence supports promotion.
6. Export only after promotion. Apply to a limited live task, then observe behavior and roll back if it regresses.

The package requires structurally distinct cases and hashes; it cannot prove that tasks are meaningfully independent or that a held-out case was kept secret. Synthetic demo scores do not establish real-model improvement.

## Grok Bot application workflow

Use a bot to propose a change and return it as data. Keep the original instructions, proposed instructions, intended benefit and testable risk together. Have your trusted evaluator and reviewer assess the candidate independently.

After local promotion, export the active configuration. The operator or an authorized adapter applies the supported fields through the bot application's documented controls, then verifies that the intended bot actually uses them. Preserve the previous exported version.

This release includes no Grok authentication, remote dispatcher, UI automation, or automatic remote profile editor. A local promotion is not proof of remote activation. If a remote update's result is uncertain, inspect the existing profile before repeating it.

## Cursor and coding agents

A coding worker can propose a skill or routing change, write a task-specific evaluator, or implement a host adapter. The worker remains a proposer unless the host separately authorizes another role. Changing a reviewer name in JSON does not establish independent review.

Do not let a candidate rewrite the rubric that grades it. An evaluator change needs its own review and versioned process outside this configuration loop.

## Pair with Agent Workbench

[Agent Workbench](../../workbench/README.md) handles bounded team routing and task state. Agent Evolution handles the lifecycle of a proposed configuration change. This distribution includes a [combined local example](../../../README.md) connecting their APIs; applying the resulting configuration to a real agent still belongs to the host.

A host can use Workbench to scope independent tasks, collect verified outcomes, and then use Evolution for a justified configuration proposal. Bind the task's inputs, outputs and review to the proposed version. Promoting a configuration does not retroactively approve prior task results.

## Rollback is an operational action

Restore a known version in the local state, export it, and reapply it through the same authorized host adapter. Verify the consumer afterward. Rolling back this package's state alone cannot reverse an email already sent, a purchase, or another external side effect.

## Measuring efficiency honestly

Compare the whole accepted task against a matched baseline, including coordination, review, retries and failed attempts. Keep prompt bytes, model tokens, cached tokens, account quota and monetary cost separate. Unknown usage stays unknown.

This initial engine's score gate supports its documented scalar comparison; additional telemetry belongs in your evaluator and evidence storage. Do not rename a smaller prompt a measured reduction in billed tokens.
